title: A Diary for a Friend
text: Omana and her best friend Radha were very excited. They were going on a train trip to Kerala! Omana was going to her grandmother's house and Radha was going with her family for a holiday. They had packed their bags and were ready to go. But just two days before their journey, Radha fell and fractured her right leg. The doctor said she could not move her leg for six weeks! Radha's family had to cancel their tickets. Radha was very sad. But Omana's Amma had an idea. 'Why don't you write down everything about your journey in a diary?' she said. Have you ever written a diary while travelling?

title: Think About It!
text: Why do you think people travel long distances in trains instead of cars or buses? What would happen if there were no trains?

content.tip: Ask students to imitate the 'chuk-chuk' sound of the train. Ask them if they have ever traveled in a train and to share their experiences.

content.title: The Long Train Journey
content.description: Imagine a long train moving like a giant iron snake across the country, crossing cities, rivers, and mountains to reach far away places.

title: Boarding the Train
text: When Omana reached the station, it was very crowded. She saw her name on the Reservation Chart. Once inside the train, they found their seats. Soon, a person in a black coat with a name tag came to check their tickets. This person is called the Ticket Collector.

content.mistake: Thinking the driver is the one who checks tickets.
content.correction: The Train Driver drives the train from the engine room. The Ticket Collector walks through the coaches to check everyone's tickets.

content.question: Who checks the tickets of passengers in a train?

title: Imagine and Reflect
text: Imagine you are sitting near the window seat of a moving train. What things would you see outside? Would the trees and houses seem to be moving backward? How would the sound of the train on the tracks feel to you? Explain it to your friend!

title: Connecting the Dots
text: Omana's journey connects Gujarat to Kerala. To go such a long distance, trains pass through many different states, cross large rivers over strong bridges, and even go through dark tunnels! As you travel from state to state, the food, language, and clothes of people change. This connects to our future chapters where we will learn about these different states.

content.title: Train Ticket Explorer
content.text: Ask your parents to show you an old train ticket or search for one online. Can you find the PNR number, the train number, and the date of journey? Try drawing a train ticket in your notebook and fill in your details!
